items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Dominic Remy was playing trumpet... I was playing saxophone.

ctx.x: But they had some tough guys around Jackson Avenue, too. I can't remember those brothers' names. But they were back around Jackson and, uh. White, wasn't it? I don't know. Jackson and Gravia, or, I mean, Jackson and Galvez, might be. I can't.

Did any band have a female vocalist around here? Um, now, uh, we had a band, let's see, uh, Sales was in that band, too. I can't think of the name. I used to have a picture. I was looking for it last week. It got, I got misplaced there. Uh, it was an organized band, too. And, uh, we had a girl play piano. She used to sing. She was a vocalist and she played piano on us there. And they had, uh, let me see what they had played, uh, played bass tuba with us. Uh, what's he, he plays string bass now. August Langwell.…
Who was the woman that played the piano?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets.

ctx.x: Well, uh, they'd have six pieces. We went to the Junk Hotel and played there. Well, he had Son Thomas playing guitar. I was playing bass. He had, uh, Dominic Remy on the trumpet. They had two trumpets. He had T-Boy Remy with him. And he had a fella called Pill on the clarinet. He died. He had a little bow-legged fella called Pill. Well, after that, well, Louis played around spot jobs around different places. And then, that's when he went up the line. Joe Oliver got with Joe Oliver. And him and Joe Oliver formed a…
And, uh, did he have a trombone down here, Louis? Used the trombone much?
